jobs.title: Drift Wood #35 · the phantom
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 19, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, chin up, unkempt dark hair falling forward, sharp jaw; CHLOE — aged 19, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders; GULLY — aged 20, stocky boy with a round face, easy slouch. CHLOE wears pixies tee tee. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: The graphic novel is mentioned for the first time. It already has a title. It changes by the fourth panel. Panel 1: a teenage boy in an overcoat clutching a spiral notebook to his chest at a cafeteria table across from a girl with eyeliner and a boy in a backwards cap (in this panel: WOOD, CHLOE, GULLY). Wood says "I've begun the real work. A graphic novel. It's called SLASH.". Panel 2: close-up of a teenage girl asking flat questions across a cafeteria table (in this panel: CHLOE). Chloe says "What's it about.". Wood says "A timber town. A crime. A man who—". Chloe says "How many pages.". Wood says "Conceptually, hundreds.". Panel 3: a boy in a backwards cap reaching for a spiral notebook that another boy pulls protectively away (in this panel: GULLY, WOOD). Gully says "Lemme see.". Wood says "It's not ready. Also the title's changing. It's called THE LONG WAY BACK now.". Panel 4: a teenage boy alone at a cafeteria table opening a spiral notebook to its first page: two pencil lines and a title crossed out twice with a third written beneath, black and white (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
